elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Operative Article IV.I now reads "The Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties.", replacing the unilateral seven-year Licensor option; retained sentences II ("extended by mutual written of the parties") and III ("by mutual agreement in writing") are consistent, so no residual unilateral or automatic renewal mechanic survives.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no automatic renewal — extension occurs only on mutual written agreement, so no renewal term length is imposed on Customer. (The finding's quote mapping is loose but the operative result is correct.)

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no automatic renewal remains, so no non-renewal notice window is needed — Licensee simply need not agree in writing.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is by mutual written agreement only, so no reminder mechanic is required. (The cited quote about the 45-day mutual-extension window does not itself create a reminder duty, but none is needed.)

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Article V.II sets user fees "during the Initial Period" with no renewal uplift or escalation mechanic, and any extension is by mutual written agreement, so any future pricing is Customer-consented.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — renewal is no longer automatic under the rendered Article IV.I.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — no renewal price-increase mechanic exists in the rendered text.

reasons: The original seven-year extension exercisable "at the option of the Licensor" was an imposed multi-year renewal (walk-away territory) and also contradicted Article IV.II and III; deleting it and substituting mutual-written-agreement renewal reaches the preferred position.

All remaining preferred and fallback elements are conditional on automatic renewal or a renewal price-increase mechanic; neither exists in the rendered text, so those conditions do not apply and the level is complete rather than incomplete.

Minimality holds: exactly one sentence was replaced with a concise substitute of comparable length; no favourable retained language (termination-for-breach right, payment-retention language, sentences II and III) was touched, and no extras such as notice procedures, caps or survival tails were added.

Intent is preserved: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created — "Initial Period" remains defined in the same sentence, and the retained mutual-extension sentences reinforce rather than contradict the new language.

Drafting note only (not a defect in the operative text): the element mapping cites unrelated quotes (e.g. the user-fee sentence for the CPI cap and the 45-day sentence for the reminder). These should be recharacterised as "condition not applicable" rather than "already met" to avoid implying the contract contains a reminder or uplift cap.
